title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. Π is a group: in the motivating case Π = π_{0,3}, the fundamental group of P^1 minus three points (free on two generators, discrete or profinite). The extension (3) is 1 → Π → Π̃ → C → 1. Here C is cyclic, generated by the image of a fixed element ρ ∈ Π̃; in the example Π̃ is the inverse image of {1, ρ, ρ²} ⊂ S_3 in the extension of S_3 by π_{0,3}. ρ acts on Π by conjugation, written ρ(g) = ρgρ^{-1}. Equation (8), the 'équation des lacets', says that ρ'_g := gρ is again a splitting of (3) of the same type. In the order-3 case this is the cocycle condition g·ρ(g)·ρ²(g) = 1, i.e. (gρ)^3 = 1.

What the previous page did. Π acts on the solutions of (8) by twisted conjugation, Θ_α : g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1}. This matches the conjugation action of Π on the splittings ρ'_g. The stabiliser of g is the centraliser Π^{ρ'_g} of the splitting ρ'_g, so the twisted-conjugating α is unique iff that centraliser is trivial.

What this page does.
(16) The whole group Π̃, not just Π, acts on splittings by conjugation. In particular ρ·ρ'_g·ρ^{-1} = (ρgρ^{-1})ρ = ρ'_{ρ(g)}. So conjugating splittings by ρ corresponds to the permutation g ↦ ρ(g) of the solution set of (8).
(17) g and ρ(g) are already Π-twisted-conjugate: ρ(g) = α g ρ(α)^{-1} with α = g^{-1}. Check: g^{-1}·g·ρ(g^{-1})^{-1} = ρ(g).
Consequences.
- The Π̃-action on splittings, equivalently on solutions of (8), is again given by Θ_α : g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1}, now with α ∈ Π̃.
- Since Π̃ is generated by Π and ρ, the Π̃-orbits coincide with the Π-orbits. In modern terms, the twisted classes (the nonabelian H^1(C, Π), i.e. Π-conjugacy classes of complements) are not refined by allowing conjugation by Π̃.
- (18) For any α ∈ Π̃, the element αρ(α)^{-1} = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} lies in Π and solves (8), being the image of the trivial solution g = 1.

Next page. Writing α = α_0 ρ^i, it is shown that αρ(α)^{-1} = α_0ρ(α_0)^{-1}, and that the representation by α ∈ Π̃ is not unique. Grothendieck then passes to a larger group E ⊃ Π̃ in which Π is normal.

Purpose. The aim is to classify solutions of the loop equation, the order-3 relation of Grothendieck–Teichmüller type, up to conjugacy, i.e. as conjugacy classes of order-3 splittings (torsion elements) in the extended group.
errors: No mathematical error. Formula (17) as transcribed ('g^α') should read α = g^{-1}; with that reading it checks out. The label '(14)' attached to Θ_α duplicates an earlier number (a slip, probably meant (14')).
Minor gap: 'classes de Π̃-conjugaison se réduisent aux classes de Π-conjugaison' tacitly uses that Π̃ is generated by Π and ρ. This holds since the quotient is cyclic generated by the image of ρ.

ideas.what: Splittings (complements) of an extension by a cyclic group, modulo conjugation, correspond to solutions of the cocycle equation modulo twisted conjugation g ↦ αgρ(α)^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1(Z/n, Π); conjugacy classes of complements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schreier; Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne, nonabelian H^1)

ideas.what: Conjugation by the whole extension group Π̃ gives the same orbits as conjugation by Π, because ρ(g) is Π-twisted-conjugate to g via α = g^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Action of the extension group on H^1 factors through the action of C on Π, which is trivial on H^1(C, Π)

ideas.what: The elements αρ(α)^{-1} with α ∈ Π̃ are the trivial-class solutions of the loop equation.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine nonabelian-cohomology bookkeeping for the cocycle (loop) equation. Its context, classifying order-3 splittings in extensions of π_{0,3}, relates to the known study of torsion in GT and in mapping class groups (e.g. work of Lochak–Schneps on conjugacy of torsion elements). Nothing on this page itself is new.
transcription_corrections: (16): the right-hand side should read ρ'_{ρ(g)}, not g'_{ρ(g)}.
(17): 'ρ(g) = g^α g ρ(α)^{-1}' should be 'ρ(g) = α g ρ(α)^{-1} avec α = g^{-1}'.
First line: likely 'En fait, non seulement le groupe Π, mais le groupe Π̃ lui-même opère par conjugaison sur l'ens des scindages de l'extension (3)'.
Middle passage: likely 'l'opération induite par ρ s'identifie à la permutation ρ de Π sur l'ens des solutions de (8)'.
